title: Spatial and Geographic SQL knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under 'Spatial and Geographic SQL'?
options: A row value from a different unrelated table
questions.explanation: The source SQL syllabus lists 'Spatial data concepts' as a subtopic of 'Spatial and Geographic SQL'; this lesson connects that point to a PostgreSQL-oriented example.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with spatial and geographic sql?
options: Add unrelated clauses until the output looks plausible.
Assume the database engines behave identically.
Skip edge-case checks because the sample returns rows.
Label specialist features by engine/version and provide a fallback when useful.
questions.answer_key: Label specialist features by engine/version and provide a fallback when useful.
questions.explanation: Label specialist features by engine/version and provide a fallback when useful. The lesson keeps the distinction between core SQL concepts and engine-specific behavior explicit.

questions.prompt: When an example related to spatial and geographic sql produces an unexpected result, what should you do first?
options: Remove constraints and access controls until the query succeeds.
Assume every SQL engine applies identical rules.
Inspect a small result, test a boundary or missing-value case, and compare it with the documented behavior.
Run the same statement repeatedly without inspecting the data.
questions.answer_key: Inspect a small result, test a boundary or missing-value case, and compare it with the documented behavior.
questions.explanation: A small, controlled test makes query behavior explainable. Inspect the data shape, conditions, NULLs, ties, plan, or transaction state that applies to the specific topic.
